simple.meaning: מָנוֹס (mânôwç) is a Hebrew action word meaning “a retreat (literally or figuratively); abstractly, a fleeing.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 8 times in 2 Samuel, Job, Psalms, Jeremiah, Amos, beginning at 2 Samuel 22:3. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מָנוֹס (H4498) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: מָנוֹס (mânôwç) / H4498 is traced through 2 Samuel 22:3, Job 11:20, Psalms 59:17, Psalms 142:5 with source-language evidence and verse context.

occurrences.englishText: God is my rock in whom I take refuge;
But the eyes of the wicked will fail.
To you, my strength, I will sing praises.
Yahweh, my strength, and my stronghold,
